questions.text: Which nerve fibers are responsible for transmitting sharp, localized pain?
questions.explanation: A-delta fibers are myelinated and transmit sharp, well-localized pain quickly. C-fibers transmit dull, aching pain more slowly.

questions.text: The spinothalamic tract carries pain signals to which structure in the brain?
questions.explanation: The spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature information from the spinal cord to the thalamus, which then relays it to the cerebral cortex.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between acute and chronic pain?
options: A. Acute pain is worse than chronic pain
B. Acute pain serves a protective function while chronic pain persists beyond healing
C. Chronic pain only occurs in elderly people
questions.explanation: Acute pain is a warning signal that protects us from harm, while chronic pain persists beyond the expected healing time and may not serve a protective purpose.

questions.text: Which branch of the autonomic nervous system is activated during the stress response to pain?
questions.explanation: The sympathetic nervous system is activated during stress and pain, triggering the 'fight or flight' response with increased heart rate and cortisol release.
